card.title: Short Story 4 — The Treasure in the Forest (H. G. Wells)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The story at a glance "The Treasure in the Forest" by H. G. Wells is an adventure story that turns on its readers: two rough seamen, Evans and Hooker, murder a Chinese man to steal his map of a buried treasure, sail to the island, find the gold — and die of the touch of it.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Greed kills — the Spanish treasure's poisoned environment punishes the treasure hunters.
Gothic atmosphere: the dead man, the lethal forest; link setting to theme.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: The twist: the 'treasure' they take is already lethal — irony of the prize being the poison; name it explicitly.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **Evans and Hooker** are less characters than instruments of greed — but Wells distinguishes them finely: Evans is the eager hand, first to the gold, first to touch the thorns; Hooker is the slower, more cautious intelligence that sees the trap a moment too late. Their difference makes the story's lesson universal: caution does not save the man who is already inside the crime.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Greed and retribution** — the central theme: the treasure's price is exact, and the collectors pay it in full; the story is a moral machine. **Colonial greed** — the Englishmen's casual entitlement to a Chinese discovery is the story's historical argument: the poison is only the island's version of the resistance the looters never expected.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. How did Evans and Hooker get the treasure map? (2 marks)** A. By murder: the Chinese man who discovered the hoard would not surrender its secret, and the two seamen took the map from him as he lay dying on the beach. The crime is the story's moral first move and the price of everything after. **Q. What did they find on the island? (2 marks)** A.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. What is the consequence of the men's greed? (2 marks) — one dies from the poisoned environment/guards' trap; the treasure destroys its seekers.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "The treasure in the forest is a moral trap as much as a physical one." Discuss. (8 marks)** A model answer works both senses of trap: the physical — the poisoned thorns planted by the treasure's owners, which kill Evans among the gold and Hooker at the boat — and the moral — the murder that purchased the map, the entitlement that never asked whose treasure it was, and the blindness…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The plot, retold with an eye on its turns The setup is a crime told in flashback: the dying Chinese man on the beach, the map he would not surrender, the two seamen who took it from him — the murder that buys the expedition. Wells gives the victim barely a paragraph, and the economy is the point: the whole imperial drama — a Chinese labourer's discovery, Englishmen's entitlement, a life taken for a piece of paper…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Irony of fate** — the master device: the men who murdered for the map die on the very spot the map led to; the treasure is gained and fatal in the same gesture. - **Foreshadowing** — the dying Chinese man's gestures toward the map, the island's too-quiet growth, the thorns noticed and dismissed: Wells marks the trap in advance and lets greed walk into it anyway.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Greed is the mechanism of doom: the treasure is guarded (poisoned by the dead Chinese crew's trap) — the island punishes covetousness; state the moral.  ·  Trick 2: Atmosphere: heat, silence, the dead bodies — the gothic detail foreshadows the ending; connect one detail to the outcome.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. How does Wells build suspense? (2 marks) — ominous setting details and the dead crew foreshadow danger before the climax.
